passage:
A museum played a radio broadcast from decades ago. The sound was unclear, and the speaker's voice cracked with static.
Students were used to clear videos and instant subtitles. At first, they found the recording hard to follow.
Then the guide explained that families once gathered around radios for news, music, and emergency information. A voice through a box could connect people who were far apart.
The students listened again, more patiently.
The old broadcast made them understand that every generation has its own "new media." What feels old now was once powerful enough to change how people imagined the world.
